newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks hit records as U.S. rate fears ease.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks hit records as U.S. rate fears ease.

text.p: Swiss shares ended moderately higher on Tuesday after fresh U.S. economic data dampened interest rate worries and gave the market a boost in the afternoon session, dealers said.
They said the market, already at record levels, was likely to continue its moderate rise until Friday's expiry of options and futures because some investors had to cover open positions.
The broad Swiss Performance Index closed up 6.10 points at a record finish of 2,555.41.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index advanced 8.1 points to 3,983.6 for another record close.
Nestle, up 14 francs to 1,466, led the actives list. Novartis fell one to 1,560 and Union Bank of Switzerland added two for 1,156.

Dealers said there was new buying interest from abroad. NatWest Securities said it put three Swiss shares on its list of 15 European stocks expected to outperform during 1997. It also picked Switzerland as a favourite market.
The three shares listed were Clariant, up 16 to 612, Credit Suisse Group, steady at 134.75, and Roche, which rose five to 10,740.
Banks, recently neglected, attracted some new interest. Swiss Bank Corp added 2.25 francs to 250.50.
